traditionalDress.men: A suriya (dhoti) with a chadar (drape) called a seleng, or simply a dhoti-kurta; the gamosa, a white handwoven cloth with a red border, is worn or carried on many social and religious occasions.
traditionalDress.women: The Mekhela Chador, a two-piece garment consisting of a cylindrical skirt (mekhela) and an upper drape (chador), traditionally handwoven from Assam silk such as muga, eri, or pat silk with intricate motifs.

festivals.name: Bihu
festivals.description: Assam's main festival, comprising three harvest-related celebrations across the year — Bohag (Rongali) Bihu marking the new year and spring, Kati Bihu, and Magh (Bhogali) Bihu — each with its own songs, dances, and rituals.

festivals.name: Ambubachi Mela
festivals.description: An annual festival at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati marking the symbolic menstruation of the goddess Kamakhya; the temple closes for three days before reopening with rituals attended by thousands of devotees.

festivals.name: Ali Aye Ligang
festivals.description: A spring sowing festival of the Mising community, celebrated with community feasts, folk songs, and the Gumrag dance.

music: Instruments include the dhol, pepa (buffalo-horn trumpet), and taal
folklore: Tejimola is a well-known Assamese folk tale about a girl mistreated and ultimately killed by her cruel stepmother, who is then reincarnated in several forms — including a plant and a bird — before her identity is restored; the story is often told as a lesson about compassion and justice.
